anomalies.GEN.728: The giant-planet and planets-per-star rates of the planet architecture (GEN.728, wired on train 4, epoch 126) against the observed bands; Planets 1 tunes the architecture toward them, so the gap is carried by GEN.728.

reference.kind: observed rates of planet_occurrence.json (READ or 2ND-HAND, tier T1 or T2)

inner_fraction.source: stars hotter than 6500 K with Kepler-like planets (Yang, Xie and Zhou 2020, arXiv:2002.02840; READ, T1)

inner_multiplicity.source: the same for stars hotter than 6500 K (Yang, Xie and Zhou 2020, arXiv:2002.02840; READ, T1)

earth_in_hz.source: planets of 0.5 to 1.5 Earth radii in the conservative habitable zone of stars of 4800 to 6300 K (the two extremes of the extrapolation, 0.37 and 0.60, are the band's ends) (Bryson et al. 2021, arXiv:2010.14812; READ, T1)

giants_2_8_au.source: giant planets (0.1 to 20 Jupiter masses) with semi-major axes of 2 to 8 AU, per FGKM star of the California Legacy Survey (Fulton et al. 2021, arXiv:2105.11584; READ, T1)

hot_jupiter_rate.source: planets of 8 to 20 Earth radii with periods under 10 days, Kepler field (Zhu and Dong 2021, arXiv:2103.02127; READ, T1); or hot Jupiters of F, G and K dwarfs of the solar neighbourhood, radial velocity (the larger of the two measured rates; Zhu and Dong 2021 give 0.9 to 1.2 percent from Wright et al. 2012) (Wright et al. 2012, arXiv:1205.2273; READ, T1)

inner_fraction.source: stars with at least one planet of radius 1 Earth radius or more and period under 400 days (Zhu et al. 2018, arXiv:1802.09526; READ, T1)

inner_multiplicity.source: mean number of Kepler-like planets (radius 1 Earth radius or more, period under 400 days) in a system that has any (Zhu et al. 2018, arXiv:1802.09526; READ, T1)

pairs_over_10_hill_radii.source: adjacent pairs in multi-planet Kepler systems at least 10 mutual Hill radii apart; the most common spacing is about 20; essentially no pair has a period ratio under 1.2 (Weiss et al. 2018, arXiv:1706.06204; READ, T1)

planets_per_star.source: planets of 1 to 20 Earth radii with periods under 400 days, per Sun-like star (Zhu and Dong 2021, ARA&A 59:291, arXiv:2103.02127 (their own analysis of the Kepler DR25 sample); READ, T1)

giants_2_8_au.source: giant planets (0.1 to 20 Jupiter masses) with semi-major axes of 2 to 8 AU, per FGKM star of the California Legacy Survey (Fulton et al. 2021, arXiv:2105.11584; READ, T1)

pairs_over_10_hill_radii.source: adjacent pairs in multi-planet Kepler systems at least 10 mutual Hill radii apart; the most common spacing is about 20; essentially no pair has a period ratio under 1.2 (Weiss et al. 2018, arXiv:1706.06204; READ, T1)

planets_per_star.source: the same for stars of 4000 to 5000 K, a factor of about 2.7 above the Sun-like sample (Zhu and Dong 2021, arXiv:2103.02127; READ, T1)

hot_jupiter_rate.source: planets of 7 Earth radii to 2 Jupiter radii with periods of 0.8 to 10 days around M dwarfs of 0.45 to 0.65 solar masses (Gan et al. 2023, arXiv:2210.08313; READ, T1)

inner_fraction.source: stars cooler than 5000 K with Kepler-like planets (radius 1 Earth radius or more, period under 400 days) (Yang, Xie and Zhou 2020, arXiv:2002.02840; READ, T1)

inner_multiplicity.source: the same for stars cooler than 5000 K (Yang, Xie and Zhou 2020, arXiv:2002.02840; READ, T1)

small_planets_per_star.source: planets of 1 to 4 Earth radii with periods under 200 days, per M dwarf (Dressing and Charbonneau 2015, arXiv:1501.01623; READ, T1)
